In the early months of the coronavirus pandemic, social media platforms were flooded with stories and images depicting acts of solidarity, hope, and religious expression among patients and healthcare workers worldwide. One particular post has circulated widely, claiming that coronavirus-positive patients in a hospital in Italy were listening to Gurbani Kirtan, a Sikh devotional music, as part of their recovery or coping process. This claim has attracted considerable attention, especially among Sikh communities and those interested in interfaith gestures during times of crisis.

To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to understand both the context of Italy’s experience during the COVID-19 pandemic and the nature of Gurbani Kirtan. Italy was among the first European countries to be severely affected by COVID-19 in early 2020, with hospitals in regions like Lombardy facing overwhelming numbers of patients. In these dire circumstances, stories of music and prayer being used to comfort patients did emerge, often featuring Italian songs, classical music, and messages of hope from hospital balconies.

Gurbani Kirtan refers to the singing of sacred hymns from the Sikh scriptures, usually performed in Gurdwaras (Sikh places of worship) or at Sikh religious gatherings. Sikh communities are present in Italy, with notable populations in regions such as Emilia-Romagna and Lombardy, many of whom work in agriculture and manufacturing. These communities have been known for their charitable efforts, including distributing food to those in need during the pandemic.

The claim that coronavirus-positive patients in an Italian hospital were listening to Gurbani Kirtan appears to stem from a viral video circulated online. In the footage, patients in a hospital ward are shown listening to Sikh hymns, with the suggestion that this was done to comfort them during their illness. However, upon closer examination, several points warrant fact-checking:

First, there is no verifiable evidence from mainstream Italian media or official hospital sources confirming that Gurbani Kirtan was played for COVID-19 patients as a hospital-sanctioned practice. The video itself lacks contextual details such as the hospital’s name, location, and dates. The presence of Sikh hymns in a hospital setting is plausible in areas with a significant Sikh population, especially if Sikh staff or volunteers were present and allowed to share their music with patients. However, such occurrences would likely be informal and not a widespread or official protocol.

Second, the video does not clarify whether the patients listening to the music were of Sikh faith or of other backgrounds. In multicultural hospital environments, it is not unusual for staff or volunteers to offer comfort through music, prayer, or other means, sometimes reflecting their own cultural or religious backgrounds.

Third, some versions of the viral video have been found to be edited or misattributed, with similar scenes of patients in hospitals paired with different audio tracks, including Sikh hymns. This raises questions about the authenticity of the original footage and its context.

In summary, while it is possible that Gurbani Kirtan was played for coronavirus-positive patients in an Italian hospital—particularly in areas with a strong Sikh presence—there is insufficient evidence to support the claim as a widespread or officially sanctioned practice. The viral video lacks clear identification and confirmation. The story resonates as a symbol of interfaith compassion during a global crisis, but its authenticity cannot be fully verified based on currently available information. As with many social media claims, viewers are encouraged to seek corroboration from reliable sources before accepting such stories as fact.

Amid the ongoing challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic, social media has played a critical role in shaping public perception and spreading information—both accurate and inaccurate. A recent post circulating online claims that people in Kolkata, India, have been breaking lockdown restrictions and pelting stones at police officers. This assertion raises concerns about public safety, adherence to government regulations, and the relationship between law enforcement and local communities during a public health emergency. In this article, we examine the validity of this claim and provide a thorough analysis of the situation.

To understand the context, it is important to recall that in response to rising COVID-19 cases, Indian authorities have periodically imposed strict lockdown measures, particularly in urban centers like Kolkata. These restrictions typically include curfews, limitations on public gatherings, and the closure of non-essential businesses. Enforcement of these measures has been primarily the responsibility of local police forces, often leading to tense interactions in densely populated neighborhoods where livelihoods have been affected.

Incidents of public unrest during lockdowns have been reported in various parts of India, including Kolkata. There have been instances where frustration over economic hardship, limited access to essential services, and perceived heavy-handedness by the police have led to confrontations. In Kolkata, several news outlets and official statements have documented cases where crowds gathered in defiance of lockdown orders, sometimes resulting in clashes with law enforcement. In some cases, these confrontations have escalated, with reports of stone-pelting by groups of individuals.

However, it is crucial to approach such claims with nuance. While isolated incidents of stone-pelting during lockdown enforcement have occurred, they have not been widespread or representative of the entire population of Kolkata. Most residents have complied with the lockdown regulations, and only a small minority have participated in such acts. Law enforcement agencies have responded by increasing patrols, making arrests, and attempting to engage with community leaders to mitigate tensions.

Social media posts, such as the one in question, often amplify specific incidents and may lack context or exaggerate the scale of unrest. Videos and images circulating online sometimes depict chaotic scenes but do not always provide accurate information on location, date, or the underlying circumstances. Fact-checking such content requires cross-verification with official statements, local news reports, and eyewitness accounts.

In summary, the claim that people in Kolkata have been breaking lockdown and pelting stones at police contains elements of truth, as there have been documented incidents of such behavior. However, these events are not indicative of widespread lawlessness—they are isolated occurrences in response to extraordinary public health measures. Most residents continue to comply with lockdown directives, and both police and community leaders are working to maintain order and safety. As always, it is essential to critically evaluate social media claims and seek comprehensive information before drawing conclusions about complex situations.

During the height of the coronavirus pandemic, public figures’ actions were scrutinized for their adherence to safety protocols and government guidelines. A social media post claims that Boris Johnson, former Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, was seen shopping in England during the pandemic. This assertion raises questions about its accuracy, the context of the event, and its implications.

To begin, Boris Johnson served as the UK’s Prime Minister from July 2019 to September 2022, overseeing the government’s response to COVID-19. The United Kingdom imposed a series of lockdowns and restrictions on public movement and activities between March 2020 and mid-2021, with regulations regularly updated in response to case numbers and scientific advice. Essential outings, including shopping for groceries and necessities, were permitted under most restrictions, provided people followed measures such as mask-wearing, social distancing, and hand hygiene.

The core claim—that Boris Johnson was shopping in England during the coronavirus pandemic—is plausible within this context. Like other citizens, government officials were allowed to shop for essentials, and Johnson was photographed in public spaces several times during the pandemic. Notably, images and videos circulated online in 2020 and 2021 showing Johnson visiting supermarkets, pharmacies, and other shops. These outings were typically linked to official duties, public messaging, or personal needs.

Fact-checking this claim requires examining when and how Johnson was seen shopping, and whether his actions complied with the prevailing COVID-19 rules. In several instances, Johnson was pictured wearing a mask and following distancing guidelines, as required by law at the time. For example, in July 2020, he was photographed wearing a mask while shopping in a London store, shortly after the government made face coverings mandatory in shops. On other occasions, Johnson participated in public service campaigns urging citizens to follow safety measures while shopping.

However, there were also moments of controversy. At times, Johnson was criticized for inconsistent mask usage or for appearing in crowded settings. Such instances sparked debate over whether he was setting the right example for the public. Nevertheless, there is no evidence to suggest that Johnson flagrantly disregarded the law or routinely violated restrictions during shopping trips.

The broader context is important: shopping was one of the few permitted activities during lockdowns, and public figures were expected to model responsible behavior. While Johnson’s appearances attracted attention, the fact that he shopped in England during the pandemic aligns with regulations in place, as long as safety protocols were observed.

In conclusion, the claim that Boris Johnson was shopping in England during the coronavirus pandemic is accurate in its basic premise. He was indeed seen shopping publicly during this period. The available evidence indicates that these outings generally complied with government guidelines, although some actions—such as inconsistent mask usage—were criticized in the media. The scrutiny surrounding such incidents reflects the heightened expectations placed on leaders during a public health crisis, underscoring the importance of transparency and accountability in times of national emergency.

During the nationwide lockdowns implemented in India to contain the spread of COVID-19, allegations arose regarding the conduct of police officers enforcing these restrictions. The claim that "police beating common people during lockdown in India" circulated widely on social media, sparking debate and concern among citizens and human rights organizations.

To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to understand the context in which these events unfolded. In March 2020, the Government of India announced a stringent nationwide lockdown, restricting public movement and closing most businesses. The lockdown aimed to curb the spread of the coronavirus by minimizing social contact. Enforcement of these orders fell largely on local police forces, who were tasked with ensuring that citizens adhered to curfews and movement restrictions.

Almost immediately after the lockdown began, videos and photographs began to surface on social media platforms, purportedly showing police officers in various cities confronting individuals on the streets. Some footage depicted officers using sticks, known as lathis, to hit people who were allegedly violating lockdown orders. In several instances, people were seen being chased, struck, or punished by being made to perform humiliating tasks. These incidents were reported in major cities such as Delhi, Mumbai, and Kolkata, as well as in smaller towns and villages.

While the authenticity of every video could not be independently verified, the recurrence of such reports from multiple regions suggested a pattern of police using physical force to enforce compliance. Interviews with affected individuals and statements from civil society groups described instances where citizens stepping out for essential reasons, such as buying food or medicine, were subjected to harsh treatment. In some cases, police action was criticized as disproportionate, particularly when directed at those who appeared to pose no immediate threat or risk.

Indian police officials responded to these allegations by stating that officers were under immense pressure to maintain public order during an unprecedented crisis. Authorities argued that some force was necessary to prevent gatherings and ensure public safety, but acknowledged that excessive use of force was not condoned. In response to widespread criticism, several state police departments issued guidelines urging officers to exercise restraint and sensitivity, especially towards vulnerable groups.

Fact-checking the core claim, evidence from news reports, eyewitness accounts, and visual documentation indicates that incidents of police beating common people during the lockdown did occur. However, it is important to note that such actions were not officially sanctioned as standard procedure, and were often the subject of condemnation by both the government and the public. The scale and frequency of these incidents varied across regions, with some areas reporting more aggressive enforcement than others.

In conclusion, the claim that police beat common people during lockdown in India is supported by documented incidents, although the extent and nature of these events differed depending on local circumstances and individual officers' conduct. The situation highlighted the challenges of balancing public health measures with civil rights, and underscored the need for accountability and oversight in law enforcement practices during times of crisis.

เจ้าหน้าที่ตำรวจของอินเดียตอบโต้ข้อกล่าวหาดังกล่าวโดยระบุว่า ผู้ปฏิบัติงานอยู่ภายใต้ความกดดันอย่างมากเพื่อรักษาความสงบสุขในช่วงวิกฤตที่ไม่เคยมีมาก่อน ทางการอ้างว่าการใช้กำลังบางอย่างจำเป็นเพื่อป้องกันการรวมตัวกันและรักษาความปลอดภัยของประชาชน แต่ก็ยอมรับว่าการใช้กำลังเกินจำเป็นไม่ได้รับการอนุญาต ในตอบโต้กับการวิจารณ์อย่างกว้างขวาง หลายหน่วยงานตำรวจของรัฐได้ออกคำแนะนำให้เจ้าหน้าที่ใช้ความระมัดระวังและมีความอ่อนน้อมถ่อมตน โดยเฉพาะกับกลุ่มที่มีความเปราะบาง

Vaishno Devi shrine, located near Katra in Jammu and Kashmir, is one of India’s most prominent Hindu pilgrimage destinations. The area surrounding the shrine is characterized by hilly terrain and dense forests, but it is not known to be a natural habitat for lions. In India, wild lions are almost exclusively found in the Gir Forest National Park and surrounding regions in the state of Gujarat, situated over a thousand kilometers from Vaishno Devi. The local fauna in and around Vaishno Devi typically includes leopards, Himalayan black bears, monkeys, and a variety of birds, but not lions.

The COVID-19 lockdown led to reduced human activity in many areas, which did result in wildlife venturing into towns and cities more frequently than usual. There have been numerous verified reports of animals, such as deer, leopards, and monkeys, appearing on empty streets during this period. However, there have been no credible reports of Asiatic lions wandering far from their established habitat in Gujarat.

Analyzing the viral content further, many such posts are often accompanied by old or unrelated footage. In cases like this, videos or photographs of lions walking on roads are sometimes taken from wildlife reserves or national parks and misattributed to locations such as Vaishno Devi for sensationalism. A close look at the visuals commonly associated with this viral post reveals that the background, road signs, and landscape do not match the geography of Jammu and Kashmir. Moreover, the physical characteristics of the road and surrounding flora are more consistent with regions in western India, such as Gujarat, where lions naturally exist.

Local authorities and wildlife experts have also weighed in, stating that there have been no confirmed sightings or official reports of lions near Vaishno Devi at any time, including during the lockdown. The Vaishno Devi shrine, while occasionally visited by wild animals, has never been known as a destination for lions.

In conclusion, the claim that a lion was walking on a road and heading to the Vaishno Devi shrine during the lockdown is not supported by the facts. The natural habitat of lions is far removed from the region, and there is no evidence to suggest such an occurrence took place. The viral post appears to be a case of misattributed or recycled footage, possibly shared for entertainment or shock value. As always, it is important to verify the origin and context of wildlife videos before accepting extraordinary claims on social media.

De corona-lockdown leidde tot een verminderde menselijke activiteit in veel gebieden, wat tot een toename van wilde dieren op straat leidde. Er zijn vele geverifieerde rapportages van dieren zoals herten, leeuwen en marmotten die tijdens deze periode op lege straten verschenen. Echter, er zijn geen betrouwbare rapportages van Asiatische leeuwen die ver van hun natuurlijke leefgebied in Gujarat wandelen.

Bij verdere analyse van de virale inhoud worden vaak veel dergelijke berichten vergezeld door oude of ongerelateerde beelden. In gevallen zoals deze worden soms beelden of foto's van leeuwen die op straat lopen genomen in wildleefgebieden of nationale parken en onjuist toegeschreven aan locaties zoals het Vaishno Devi voor sensatie. Een nauwkeurige bekijking van de visuele elementen die vaak aan deze virale post zijn verbonden, toont aan dat de achtergrond, wegplaten en landschap niet overeenkomen met de geografie van Jammu en Kashmir. Bovendien zijn de fysieke kenmerken van de weg en de omringende flora meer consistent met regio's in westelijk India, zoals Gujarat, waar leeuwen natuurlijk voorkomen.

De lokale autoriteiten en dierendienstexperts hebben ook betoond dat er geen bevestigde waarnemingen of officiële rapportages zijn van leeuwen in de buurt van het Vaishno Devi op welke momenten dan ook, inclusief tijdens de lockdown. Het Vaishno Devi-verblijf, dat soms wordt bezocht door wilde dieren, is nooit bekend geweest als een bestemming voor leeuwen.

In afsluiting op dit onderzoek is de bewering dat een leeuw op straat liep en naar het Vaishno Devi-verblijf ging tijdens de lockdown niet onderbouwd door feiten. Het natuurlijke leefgebied van leeuwen ligt ver buiten de regio, en er is geen bewijs dat dergelijke gebeurtenis heeft plaatsgevonden. De virale post lijkt een geval van onjuist toegeschreven of gerecycled beelden te zijn, mogelijk gedeeld voor entertainment of schokwaarde. Zoals altijd is het belangrijk om de oorsprong en context van dierbeelden te controleren voordat u ongewone claims op sociale media accepteert.

In recent days, a social media post has circulated claiming that trucks are transporting the bodies of patients who have died from coronavirus. This assertion has generated significant concern and discussion online, with many questioning its accuracy and implications. To clarify the facts surrounding this claim, we examine the context, background, and the reality of how the COVID-19 pandemic has affected the handling of deceased individuals.

The core claim suggests that trucks are being used to carry the bodies of coronavirus victims. This notion evokes images of mass casualties and overwhelmed systems, raising anxiety about the severity of the pandemic and the capacity of health and mortuary services to cope with rising deaths.

During the initial waves of the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly in areas with high rates of infection and mortality, hospitals and mortuaries faced unprecedented challenges. In cities such as New York, there were reports and documented instances where refrigerated trucks were used as temporary morgues. The surge in patient deaths outpaced the ability of traditional morgue facilities to store bodies, leading officials to deploy trucks equipped with refrigeration units to store the remains safely until they could be processed and either buried or cremated.

It is important to note that the use of trucks in this context did not represent a routine or standard practice prior to the pandemic. Instead, it was an emergency measure implemented under dire circumstances to ensure that the dignity and safety of the deceased and those handling them were maintained. The bodies transported in these trucks were typically handled with care, and the process was overseen by health and city officials in accordance with legal and health protocols.

While the social media post may be interpreted as sensational or alarming, it does reflect a reality that occurred in specific locations and under extraordinary conditions. Trucks were indeed used to carry the bodies of patients who died from coronavirus, most notably during periods when healthcare facilities were overwhelmed and traditional mortuary resources were insufficient. However, this was not a universal or permanent approach, but rather a temporary solution in response to a crisis.

As the pandemic progressed and systems adapted, the reliance on refrigerated trucks diminished. Hospitals and city officials improved procedures for handling the deceased, and additional resources were allocated to manage surges in mortality. The use of such trucks became less common as the situation stabilized in many regions.

In summary, the core claim that trucks are carrying dead bodies of coronavirus patients is factually accurate but requires context to be fully understood. The use of trucks for this purpose was a direct response to the overwhelming number of deaths in certain areas during the peak of the pandemic. It was implemented to preserve public health, dignity, and safety, and was not indicative of standard procedures outside of emergency situations. While the imagery may be unsettling, the reality underscores the immense challenges faced by communities during the COVID-19 crisis and the extraordinary measures taken to address them.

A recent social media post claims that people in Chandni Chowk market are breaking COVID-19 lockdown restrictions due to Eid celebrations. This assertion has stirred debate online, raising concerns about public health, compliance with government regulations, and the role of religious festivals during the pandemic. This article examines the claim in detail, providing context, background, and analysis to determine its accuracy.

Chandni Chowk, located in the heart of Old Delhi, is one of India's oldest and busiest markets. The area is well-known for its diverse commercial activity, drawing locals and tourists alike, especially during major festivals. Eid, a significant festival for the Muslim community, often sees increased crowds in markets as people shop for food, clothing, and gifts.

The COVID-19 pandemic led the Indian government to impose phased lockdowns and restrictions across the country, including Delhi. During lockdown periods, non-essential businesses were ordered to close, and public gatherings were restricted to curb the spread of the virus. Authorities have, at various times, announced intensified enforcement around festival periods, recognizing the potential for increased gatherings.

To analyze the claim that Chandni Chowk market is seeing lockdown violations because of Eid, it is important to consider several factors:

First, the timing of the post is crucial. If the claim was made during an official lockdown or during periods of strict curfews, authorities would have been expected to enforce regulations in busy areas like Chandni Chowk. Historical reports indicate that markets in Delhi, including Chandni Chowk, have experienced sporadic crowding during festival seasons. However, such gatherings are not limited to Eid alone; other festivals, such as Diwali and Holi, have also seen similar patterns.

Second, the claim attributes the lockdown violations specifically to Eid. While it is true that Eid can lead to increased footfall in marketplaces, attributing the violations solely to the festival overlooks other contributing factors. For example, Chandni Chowk serves a wide demographic, and commercial activity does not cease during other festivals or even in the absence of a festival. The relaxation of restrictions, confusion regarding guidelines, and economic pressure on traders to resume business have also played roles in crowd formation.

Third, enforcement of lockdowns has varied based on government directives and public compliance. Visual evidence from news outlets and social media around major festivals has shown instances of crowding and lapses in social distancing, with some images depicting people shopping during lockdowns. However, these incidents have involved people from diverse backgrounds and have not been limited to one community or festival.

Lastly, authorities have periodically taken measures to control crowds in Chandni Chowk by deploying police personnel, barricading certain areas, and issuing fines for violations. Public messaging has stressed the importance of adhering to COVID-19 protocols during all festivals, including Eid.

In conclusion, while it is accurate that Chandni Chowk market has experienced crowding and lockdown violations during festival periods, attributing these solely to Eid oversimplifies the issue. The phenomenon of lockdown breaches in busy markets is multifaceted, involving a mix of festival-driven shopping, economic necessity, and varying enforcement. The claim that people in Chandni Chowk are breaking lockdown because of Eid contains a kernel of truth regarding increased activity, but does not fully account for the broader context of market behavior during the pandemic.

A claim circulating on social media asserts that UNICEF has stated the novel coronavirus, SARS-CoV-2, remains on human hands for 10 minutes. This post has generated considerable attention, especially among individuals concerned about personal hygiene and transmission risks during the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. However, a review of available information and official guidance reveals that this claim is misleading.

To understand the validity of the statement, it is necessary to clarify a few points. First, UNICEF, the United Nations Children's Fund, is a reputable international organization dedicated to advocating for children’s rights and wellbeing. Since the emergence of COVID-19, UNICEF has actively participated in disseminating accurate information about the virus, prevention measures, and public health guidelines. Their communications have focused on handwashing, mask usage, and social distancing to curb the spread of the virus.

The central claim in the social media post is twofold: that the coronavirus remains on hands for exactly ten minutes, and that this assertion originates from UNICEF. An examination of UNICEF’s official advice and published materials does not yield any statement specifying a ten-minute timeframe for the virus to survive on human skin. Instead, health organizations, including UNICEF, emphasize the importance of frequent and proper handwashing with soap and water for at least 20 seconds, or using hand sanitizer with at least 60% alcohol, to effectively remove or deactivate the virus.

The survivability of SARS-CoV-2 on skin and surfaces has been the subject of scientific inquiry. Studies have shown that the virus can remain viable on various surfaces for hours or even days under specific conditions. However, the exact duration the virus survives on human skin is variable and depends on environmental factors such as temperature, humidity, and skin cleanliness. Laboratory experiments have suggested that the virus can persist on skin for several hours under controlled conditions, but these results do not necessarily translate to real-world scenarios.

The claim that the virus “stays in hands for 10 minutes” may stem from attempts to simplify complex scientific findings or from misinterpretations of public health messaging. There is no evidence to support the notion that the virus only remains on hands for a fixed ten-minute period before disappearing. Moreover, the origin attributed to UNICEF appears unfounded; the organization’s guidance does not mention such a specific duration.

In summary, the claim that UNICEF has stated the novel coronavirus remains on hands for 10 minutes is inaccurate. UNICEF’s advice centers on the importance of regular hand hygiene without specifying a precise timeframe for viral survival on skin. The survivability of the virus on human hands is variable and context-dependent, and public health recommendations are designed to reduce the risk of transmission through effective cleaning practices rather than reliance on time-based assumptions. Individuals are encouraged to follow established guidelines from reputable sources to protect themselves and others during the pandemic.

اصلی که در شبکه‌های اجتماعی مطرح شده است، ادعا می‌کند که سازمان بین‌المللی کودکان (UNICEF) اعلام کرده است که ویروس جدید کرونا (SARS-CoV-2) به مدت ده دقیقه روی دست‌های انسانی باقی می‌ماند. این پست توجه زیادی را به خود جذب کرده است، به خصوص در میان افرادی که به بهداشت شخصی و خطرات انتقال در دوران شیوع بیماری کرونا علاقه‌مند هستند. با این حال، بررسی اطلاعات موجود و دستورالعمل‌های رسمی نشان می‌دهد که این ادعا نادرست است.

برای درک اعتبار این اظهار نظر، لازم است چند نکته را واضح کنیم. اول، سازمان بین‌المللی کودکان (UNICEF) یک سازمان بین‌المللی با اهمیت است که به دفاع از حقوق و سلامت کودکان می‌پردازد. از شروع بیماری کرونا، UNICEF به طور فعال در پخش اطلاعات دقیق درباره ویروس، اقدامات جلوگیری و دستورالعمل‌های بهداشتی شرکت کرده است. ارتباطات آنها به مسائلی مانند شستشوی دست، استفاده از ماسک و فاصله گذاری اجتماعی متمرکز شده است تا انتشار ویروس را کنترل کند.

ادعای اصلی در پست شبکه‌های اجتماعی دو جزء است: اول، اینکه ویروس کرونا به مدت دقیقاً ده دقیقه روی دست‌های انسانی باقی می‌ماند، و دوم اینکه این ادعا از سوی UNICEF ارائه شده است. بررسی دستورالعمل‌های رسمی و مواد منتشر شده UNICEF، هیچ اظهار نظری درباره یک دوره زمانی مشخص 10 دقیقه برای باقی ماندن ویروس روی پوست انسانی نشان نمی‌دهد. به جای آن، سازمان‌های بهداشتی، شامل UNICEF، بر اهمیت شستشوی دست با شامپو و آب به مدت حداقل 20 ثانیه یا استفاده از آنتی بکتریال با حداقل 60 درصد الکل برای حذف یا غیر فعال کردن ویروس تأکید می‌کنند.

میزان باقی ماندن SARS-CoV-2 روی پوست و سطوح مختلف موضوع تحقیقات علمی است. مطالعات نشان می‌دهند که ویروس می‌تواند به مدت ساعات یا حتی روزها در شرایط خاص روی سطوح باقی بماند. با این حال، مدت زمان دقیقی که ویروس روی پوست انسانی باقی می‌ماند متغیر است و به عوامل محیطی مانند دمای محیط، رطوبت و تمیزی پوست بستگی دارد. آزمایشات آزمایشگاهی نشان می‌دهد که ویروس می‌تواند در شرایط کنترل شده به مدت چند ساعت روی پوست باقی بماند، اما این نتایج حتماً به شرایط واقعی تبدیل نمی‌شوند.

به طور خلاصه، ادعا که UNICEF اعلام کرده است ویروس جدید کرونا به مدت ده دقیقه روی دست‌های انسانی باقی می‌ماند، نادرست است. دستورالعمل‌های UNICEF به اهمیت شستشوی دست‌ها با یک دوره منظم اشاره دارد، بدون اینکه مدت زمان مشخصی برای باقی ماندن ویروس روی پوست را تعیین کند. میزان باقی ماندن ویروس روی دست‌های انسانی متغیر است و به شرایط ویژه بستگی دارد، و دستورالعمل‌های بهداشتی به منظور کاهش خطر انتقال از طریق اقدامات تمیزی موثر طراحی شده‌اند، نه اینکه به فرضیه‌های زمانی وابسته باشند. افراد بهتر است دستورالعمل‌های معتبر را از منابع معتبر در طول بیماری کرونا دنبال کنند تا خود و دیگران را در برابر این بیماری حفظ کنند.

A social media post claiming that all employees of the Punjab National Bank (PNB) branch in Loni have tested positive for coronavirus has garnered significant attention and concern online. Given the sensitivity of public health issues and the potential impact on local communities, it is important to examine the accuracy of this claim and provide clear information.

To understand the context, Loni is a town situated in the Ghaziabad district of Uttar Pradesh, bordering the national capital, Delhi. Punjab National Bank is one of India’s largest public sector banks, with numerous branches serving both urban and rural areas. During the COVID-19 pandemic, banks, like other essential services, remained operational, often with strict protocols to safeguard staff and customers.

The claim that all employees of a specific branch have contracted the virus is alarming, as it suggests a possible outbreak at a critical public service point. If true, such an event would likely necessitate the immediate closure of the branch, notification of customers, contact tracing, and potentially wider testing of those who visited the branch recently. News of such an incident would also prompt local authorities to issue public advisories and initiate containment measures.

Upon investigation, there is no official confirmation from PNB or local health authorities that all employees at the Loni branch have tested positive for COVID-19. In the past, there have been instances where individual bank branches across India reported cases among staff, leading to temporary closures and sanitization. However, reports of an entire branch’s workforce being infected are rare and typically attract prompt action and widespread media coverage.

Fact-checking such claims involves checking for multiple credible sources, including local news outlets, government health bulletins, and official bank statements. As of now, no accredited news organization has reported a mass outbreak at the PNB Loni branch. Additionally, neither the district health department nor the bank’s regional office has issued any alerts or advisories regarding the alleged incident.

It is possible that the claim originated from confusion or misinterpretation of events. For instance, if a few staff members tested positive, rumors can quickly escalate on social media, leading to exaggerated posts. During the COVID-19 pandemic, misinformation about infection clusters and closures has been widespread, sometimes causing unnecessary panic among the public.

In summary, the assertion that all employees of the PNB Loni branch have tested positive for coronavirus is not supported by any official evidence or credible reporting as of now. While isolated cases among staff members are plausible, a complete infection of the workforce would have resulted in swift public notification and intervention, which has not occurred. The public is advised to rely on verified information from official sources and exercise caution when sharing unconfirmed news, especially in matters related to public health.

article_content:
A social media post recently circulated showing an image of parrots eating from an open rice bag, accompanied by the claim: “Parrots eating from rice bag due to lockdown.” The post suggests that lockdown measures, presumably related to the COVID-19 pandemic, have driven the birds to seek food in unusual places. This article examines the accuracy of this claim, analyzes the context, and considers the broader implications for both wildlife and human communities.

Background and Context

During the COVID-19 pandemic, many countries imposed strict lockdowns to curb the spread of the virus. These measures included the closure of markets, restrictions on outdoor movement, and the temporary shuttering of restaurants and food stalls. In many urban and suburban areas, these changes had a noticeable impact on local wildlife. Reports emerged of wild animals venturing into less-populated streets and birds flocking to new areas in search of food.

Parrots, known for their intelligence and adaptability, are commonly found in several regions, particularly in South and Southeast Asia. They are regular visitors to farmlands, markets, and homes, often attracted by grains and seeds. The image in question, depicting parrots gathered around a rice bag, appears to reinforce the narrative that lockdowns forced these birds to change their feeding habits.

Fact-Checking the Core Claim

To verify the claim, it is essential to consider several factors: the authenticity of the image, the behavior of parrots, and the direct impact of lockdowns on their food sources.

First, images of parrots feeding from rice bags are not uncommon and have been documented well before the pandemic. In many rural and peri-urban areas, it is typical for parrots and other grain-eating birds to forage in and around human settlements, especially where food is stored in the open or semi-open conditions. Such behavior is part of their natural adaptation to environments where agriculture and human habitation overlap.

Second, while lockdowns did reduce human activity in public spaces, they did not necessarily increase the availability of food for wildlife. In fact, reduced human presence in markets and temples—places where birds commonly scavenge food scraps—could have led some species to look elsewhere for sustenance. However, there is limited evidence to suggest a sudden, widespread change in parrot feeding behavior directly attributable to lockdowns. In many cases, parrots continued to frequent the same locations, such as farms and grain storage areas, regardless of the pandemic.

Analysis

The claim that parrots are eating from rice bags “due to lockdown” simplifies a more complex picture. While it is plausible that some birds might have sought alternative food sources during periods of reduced human activity, the behavior of parrots feeding from rice bags is not unique to the lockdown era. Rather, it reflects longstanding interactions between parrots and human food storage practices.

Conclusion

In summary, the social media post captures a genuine and common sight but overstates the causal link between lockdown measures and parrot feeding habits. Parrots have long adapted to feed on stored grains, and while the pandemic may have influenced the dynamics of human-wildlife interaction in some ways, there is no clear evidence that it significantly altered this particular behavior. The image serves as a reminder of the ongoing relationship between humans and wildlife, which extends beyond times of crisis.

Sosial media-da son dəfə dövrənən bir məqalə, parçaların açıq rizə qutusundan yemək yeyəndən bir şəkil ilə birlikdə "Koronavirus pandemiyası ilə bağlı kəsildikdən sonra parçalar rizə qutusundan yemək yeyir" deyən ifadə ilə birlikdə paylaşıldı. Məqalə, bu qədər də kəsildikdən sonra parçaların yemək qaynaqlarını təklif etmək üçün təsadüfi yerlərə məcburiyyətə məruz qaldığını iddia edir. Bu məqalə, bu iddianın doğru olub olmadığını, mənadağını və təbiət və insan toplumları üçün daha genel təsirləri nəzərdən keçirir.

Təqdim edilən məlumat və kontekst

Koronavirus pandemiyası zamanı bir çox ölkələr, vəirin yayılmasını azaltmaq üçün qeyri-adi kəsildiklər tətbiq etdi. Bu qaydalara əsasən, bazarlar bağlandı, kəsildiklər zamanı xaricdən hərəkət etmək məcburiyyətində qaldı, və təsadüfən restoranlar və yemək dəfələri kəsildi. Bir çox şəhər və ya qəsəbə ərazilərində, bu dəyişikliklər yerli təbiətə də təsir göstərdi. Yeni bir məlumat, təbiət ərazilərindən az əhalisi olan yolları və parçaların yemək qaynaqlarını arayış etməyə başladığını göstərdi.

Parçalar, əlçatmazlıq və adaptasiya qabiliyyətli heyvanlardır və müxtəlif ərazilərdə, xüsusən Cənub və Cənub-Şərq Asiyasında yaygındır. Onlar, əsasən, tarım sahələri, bazarlar və evlərdən yemək qaynaqları ilə məşğul olurlar, çünki onlar çox sayda növ dəniz mədənindən və tərəvəzlərdən yemək yeyirlər. Məsuliyyətli əsas məqalədə, parçaların rizə qutusundan yemək yeyəndən bir şəkil var və bu, kəsildiklər nəticəsində bu heyvanların yemək qaynaqlarını dəyişməyə məcburiyyətindən əlavə edir.

İddiyanın səhvini yoxlama

İddiyanın doğruluğunu təsdiqləmək üçün bir neçə amilə diqqət yetirmək vacibdir: şəklin doğruluğu, parçaların davranışları və kəsildiklərin onların yemək qaynaqlarına doğrudan təsiri.

İlk öncə, parçaların rizə qutusundan yemək yeyəndən şəkillər pandemiyadan əvvəl də mövcuddur. Bir çox qəsəbə və ya ərazilərdə, parçalar və digər növ yemək yeyən heyvanlar, yemək qaynaqları açıq və ya yarı-əlçatmaz şəkildə saxlanılan yerlərdən, insan əsaslı qurumlarla əlaqədən əlçatmazlıq etmək üçün yemək yeyirlər. Bu davranış, tarım və insan istirahəti tərəfindən əlaqəli olan mühəndisliklərin əsasında əlçatmazlıq qabiliyyəti ilə əlaqədədir.

İkinci, kəsildiklər, əhalinin xaricdəki məkanlarda hərəkətini azaldı, lakin onların təbiət üçün yemək qaynaqlarının artmasına səbəb olmazdı. Əksinə, bazarlar və məscidlərdə, parçaların yemək qalıqlarını topladığı yerlərdən əhalinin azalması, bir neçə növün yemək qaynaqlarını arayış etməyə məcburiyyətindən əlavə edir. Lakin, kəsildiklərin parçaların yemək qaynaqlarını dəyişməyə səbəb olduğu barədə əhəmiyyətli məlumat yoxdur. Əksinə, bir çox hallarda parçalar, tarım sahələri və yemək saxlama yerləri kimi eyni yerlərdə davam edir, pandemiyadan asılı olmayaraq.

Tədqiqat

"Parçalar rizə qutusundan yemək yeyir" iddiası, kəsildiklərin parçaların yemək qaynaqlarını dəyişməyə səbəb olduğu kimi səhv bir mənadağına səbəb olur. Lakin, əhalinin hərəkətində azalma zamanı bir neçə parçanın alternativ yemək qaynaqlarını arayış etməsi mümkündür. Lakin, parçaların rizə qutusundan yemək yeyəndən davranışları, kəsildiklər dövründən əvvəl də mövcuddur. Bu, parçaların insan yemək saxlama praksisləri ilə əlaqədən əlçatmazlıq qabiliyyəti ilə bağlı uzun müddət davam edən bir mənadaqdır.

Sonuç

Kəsildiklər dövründə parçaların rizə qutusundan yemək yeyəndən şəkildən əlavə edilən məlumat, bir neçə təbiət və insan əlaqəsi ilə bağlı əhəmiyyətli bir mənadaqdır. Parçalar, uzun müddət əlçatmazlıq qabiliyyəti ilə yemək saxlama qaynaqlarını yeyir və pandemiya, insan və təbiət əlaqələrini bir neçə mənada dəyişdirməyə səbəb olub. Lakin, bu mənadaqdakı davranışın əsasında bir neçə əhəmiyyətli təsir yoxdur. Bu şəkil, qeyri-adi vaxtların ötən zamanı də müxtəlif insan və təbiət əlaqələrinin mövcudluğunu nəzərdən keçirməyə kömək edir.

During the COVID-19 pandemic, India implemented one of the world’s largest and strictest lockdowns beginning in March 2020. The nationwide shutdown, designed to curb the spread of the virus, had profound economic and social consequences, particularly for vulnerable groups such as migrant workers. Amidst these hardships, claims have circulated on social media alleging that families of poor migrants committed suicide during the lockdown in India. This article examines the accuracy of this claim, providing context, background, and a fact-based analysis.

Background: The Plight of Migrant Workers During Lockdown

India’s lockdown brought the country to a sudden standstill. Factories, construction sites, and other workplaces closed, leaving millions of daily wage workers—many of whom were migrants from rural regions—without income or means to support their families. With public transportation halted and borders sealed, vast numbers of migrant workers attempted to return to their home villages on foot, often walking hundreds of kilometers.

During the nationwide lockdown period in India, a social media post began circulating, claiming that a leopard was seen roaming in Delhi’s Dwarka locality. The post, shared widely across platforms such as Twitter, Facebook, and WhatsApp, included images and videos purportedly showing a large feline wandering the streets of the residential area. This claim has generated considerable interest and concern among residents and netizens alike, prompting discussions about wildlife movement in urban spaces during the lockdown.

To assess the veracity of this claim, it is important to consider both the context of the lockdown and the background of wildlife sightings in metropolitan areas. In 2020, India imposed a strict lockdown to curb the spread of COVID-19, resulting in deserted streets and reduced human activity in cities. During this period, several reports emerged from across the country of wild animals venturing into urban environments. These included sightings of deer, peacocks, and other species in places where they are rarely seen. The absence of humans and vehicles appeared to encourage wildlife to explore areas previously dominated by people.

Dwarka, located in the southwestern part of Delhi, is a densely populated residential and commercial hub. While Delhi does have some green belts and forested areas, it is not typically known for leopard populations. Leopards are usually found in the forested fringes of the city, such as the Ridge area, and in national parks or sanctuaries located outside the metropolitan boundaries. Sightings of leopards in the core urban areas of Delhi are extremely rare and tend to attract significant attention from local authorities and media outlets.

The viral post about a leopard in Dwarka included grainy video footage and unclear images. Upon closer inspection, fact-checkers and wildlife experts analyzed the available material. Several observations emerged: the animal depicted did resemble a large cat, but some aspects of its physical features were inconsistent with those of a leopard. The videos often lacked clear landmarks or indicators that would confirm their location as Dwarka, Delhi. Furthermore, no official reports from the Delhi Forest Department or local police were released confirming the presence of a leopard in the area during the time in question.

In many previous instances, social media posts about wild animals in urban settings have been found to be either old, misattributed, or from entirely different locations. In some cases, footage from other cities or countries has been circulated with false claims about local sightings. This tendency for misinformation is heightened during periods of crisis or unusual circumstances, such as the COVID-19 lockdown.

Based on the available evidence, there is no substantiated proof that a leopard was roaming the streets of Dwarka, Delhi, during the lockdown period. While the lockdown did lead to increased wildlife movement in some areas, the specific claim regarding a leopard in this locality cannot be verified and appears to be either a misattribution or an instance of viral misinformation. Residents are advised to rely on official sources and exercise caution before spreading unverified wildlife sightings on social media.

در دوره قفل گذاری کشوری در هند، یک پست در شبکه‌های اجتماعی شیوع پیدا کرد که ادعا می‌کرد یک گرگ سیاه در محلی به نام دوارکا در دهلی مشاهده شده است. این پست که در پلتفرم‌هایی مانند توییتر، فیسبوک و واتس اپ به وسیله هزاران نفر به اشتراک گذاشته شد، شامل تصاویر و ویدئوهایی بود که به نظر می‌رسید این ویدئوها به تصویر کشیدن یک سگ فلزی بزرگ در خیابان‌های محلی مسکونی اشاره دارد. این ادعا از سوی ساکنان و کاربران شبکه‌های اجتماعی به شدت توجه و نگرانی ایجاد کرده است و بحث‌هایی درباره حرکت جانوران در فضاهای شهری در دوره قفل گذاری ایجاد کرده است.

برای ارزیابی صحت این ادعا، لازم است هم از زمینه قفل گذاری و هم از تاریخچه دیده شدن جانوران در مناطق شهری احاطه شویم. در سال ۲۰۲۰، هند قفل گذاری سختی را برای کنترل پخش کرونا به اجرا درآورد که باعث تهی شدن خیابان‌ها و کاهش فعالیت انسانی در شهرها شد. در این دوره، گزارشاتی از پراکنده شدن جانوران دیگر به مناطق شهری در سراسر کشور به نمایش گذاشته شد. این شامل دیده شدن گوسفند، فیل و گونه‌های دیگر در محلی که به ندرت این جانوران در آن مشاهده می‌شود بود. حضور کمتر انسان و وسایل نقلیه به نظر می‌رسید جانوران را تشویق کرده باشد تا مناطقی را که قبلاً توسط انسان‌ها به طور غالب حاکم بود، بررسی کنند.

دوارکا، در بخش جنوب غربی دهلی، یک مرکز مسکونی و تجاری چگال است. در حالی که دهلی از مناطق گیاهی و جنگلی نیز برخوردار است، اما به طور معمول به عنوان منطقه ای که جمعیت گرگ سیاه در آن وجود دارد شناخته نمی‌شود. گرگ سیاه معمولاً در حاشیه جنگلی شهر، مانند منطقه ریدج، و در پارک‌های ملی یا مکان‌های مسکونی خارج از مرز شهری یافت می‌شود. دیده شدن گرگ سیاه در مناطق شهری اصلی دهلی بسیار نادر است و معمولاً توجه قابل توجهی از مقامات محلی و رسانه‌ها جذب می‌کند.

پست ویروسی درباره یک گرگ سیاه در دوارکا شامل ویدئوهایی با کیفیت ضعیف و تصاویری ناوضوح بود. پس از بررسی دقیق، تحلیلگران و متخصصان جانوران به محتوای موجود نگاه کردند. چند مشاهده به نمایش گذاشته شد: جانور نشان داده شده به نظر می‌رسید یک سگ فلز بزرگ باشد، اما برخی ویژگی‌های فیزیکی آن با ویژگی‌های گرگ سیاه هماهنگ نبود. ویدئوهای معمولاً از نشانه‌هایی که می‌توانست مکان واقعی آن را به دوارکا، دهلی، اثبات کند، کمتر بود. علاوه بر این، هیچ گزارشی از وزارت جنگل و منابع طبیعی دهلی یا پلیس محلی در مورد حضور یک گرگ سیاه در آن منطقه در زمان مورد نظر منتشر نشده بود.

در بسیاری از موارد پیشین، پست‌های شبکه‌های اجتماعی درباره جانوران در محیط شهری به طور معمول یا قدیمی بوده یا به نادرستی به محل نسبت داده شده یا از محل‌های کاملاً متفاوتی می‌آید. در برخی موارد، ویدئوهایی از شهرهای دیگر یا کشورهای دیگر با ادعاهای غلط درباره مشاهدات محلی در شبکه‌های اجتماعی پخش شده است. این نیز افزایش احتمال انتشار اطلاعات غلط در دوره‌هایی مانند قفل گذاری یا شرایط نادرست دیگر است.

بر اساس شواهد موجود، هیچ اثباتی وجود ندارد که در دوره قفل گذاری، یک گرگ سیاه در خیابان‌های دوارکا، دهلی مشاهده شده باشد. در حالی که قفل گذاری باعث افزایش حرکت جانوران در برخی مناطق شده است، اما ادعای خاص درباره یک گرگ سیاه در این محل به طور قطع قابل تأیید نیست و به نظر می‌رسد این ادعا یا به نادرستی به محل نسبت داده شده یا یک مثال از انتشار اطلاعات غلط در شبکه‌های اجتماعی است. ساکنان به نفع اطلاعات رسمی و در صورت احتمال، به اشتراک گذاشتن مشاهدات غیرقابل تأیید جانوران در شبکه‌های اجتماعی دقت کنند.

As India grappled with waves of COVID-19, government authorities implemented strict lockdown measures in 2020 and 2021 to curb the spread of the virus. These lockdowns included restrictions on public gatherings, closure of markets, and limits on religious activities. The Jama Masjid area in Old Delhi, known for its bustling market and the iconic mosque, is a focal point during major Islamic festivals, particularly Eid.

A recent social media post claims that people in the Jama Masjid market broke the Indian COVID-19 lockdown due to Eid celebrations. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to consider the context of the lockdowns, the nature of Eid in India, and the situation in Delhi during the relevant period.

Eid, both Eid-ul-Fitr and Eid-ul-Adha, are significant religious festivals for Muslims in India and are typically marked by congregational prayers, shopping for festive goods, and communal gatherings. Jama Masjid, one of the largest mosques in India, attracts thousands of worshippers during Eid. The adjacent market is a popular destination for shopping, particularly ahead of the festival.

During the peak of the pandemic, Delhi was subjected to a series of lockdowns. The Delhi government announced complete lockdowns at various points, including around major festivals, to prevent mass gatherings that could accelerate the spread of COVID-19. These measures included shuttering markets, imposing curfews, and restricting religious gatherings.

Fact-checking the claim requires examining news reports, official statements, and eyewitness accounts from the period around Eid during the lockdown. Several instances were reported in mainstream media where crowds gathered in the Jama Masjid market ahead of Eid, despite restrictions. Images and videos circulated online showed people shopping for clothes, food items, and other festival essentials. In some cases, social distancing norms and mask mandates were not strictly followed.

However, authorities did respond to these incidents. Police and local administration increased patrolling and, in some cases, temporarily closed market areas to disperse crowds. Announcements were made urging people to stay indoors and follow COVID-19 protocols. The mosque itself issued advisories, and religious leaders appealed to worshippers to adhere to government guidelines.

It is important to note that while there were instances of lockdown violations in the Jama Masjid market during Eid, similar patterns were observed in other parts of Delhi and India, particularly in markets and places of worship ahead of major festivals. The violations were not unique to Jama Masjid or the Muslim community; rather, they reflected broader challenges in enforcing restrictions during significant cultural and religious events.

In conclusion, the core claim of the social media post—that people in Jama Masjid market broke the Indian COVID-19 lockdown due to Eid—has a factual basis. There were documented cases of crowds gathering in the market during the lockdown, apparently linked to Eid preparations. Nonetheless, these events were part of a wider struggle to enforce lockdown measures across diverse communities and regions during festive periods. Authorities did act to control the situation, but the challenges of managing public behavior during major festivals were evident throughout the country.

article_content:
During the nationwide COVID-19 lockdown in India, one of the most striking and tragic images was that of migrants attempting to journey home from major urban centers such as Mumbai. The viral social media post stating “Migrants traveling to their homes from Mumbai during lockdown” refers to an actual and significant event that unfolded during the first half of 2020. This article examines the claim, provides context, and investigates the accuracy of the statement.

Background and Context

India imposed a strict nationwide lockdown beginning on March 25, 2020, in an effort to curb the spread of the coronavirus. The lockdown led to the closure of most businesses, public transport, and services, effectively halting economic activity. The abruptness of the announcement left millions of daily wage workers, many of whom are migrants from various states, stranded in cities like Mumbai, Delhi, and others. With no income, limited access to shelter, and growing uncertainty about the duration of restrictions, these workers faced immense hardship.

Mumbai, home to a large population of migrant workers from states such as Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Jharkhand, and Odisha, became one of the focal points of the crisis. Migrants, mostly employed in construction, hospitality, and informal sectors, found themselves out of work and without the means to support themselves or their families.

Verification and Analysis of the Claim

The core claim that migrants traveled to their homes from Mumbai during the lockdown is accurate. This movement was both spontaneous and, at times, organized. In the initial weeks of the lockdown, with public transport shut down, thousands of migrants began walking, cycling, or hitching rides on trucks and other vehicles, attempting to cover hundreds, sometimes thousands, of kilometers to reach their native villages. Photographs and reports from Mumbai’s railway stations, bus depots, and highways showed large crowds of migrants, often carrying belongings or children, embarking on their journey home.

The government later initiated special measures to address the crisis, including the introduction of “Shramik Special” trains and buses to facilitate the movement of migrant workers. Nevertheless, logistical challenges, limited availability of transport, and confusion about registration procedures meant that many migrants continued to travel on foot or by other means.

The plight of migrants during the lockdown was widely reported, highlighting stories of hardship, exhaustion, and in some tragic cases, loss of life due to accidents and dehydration. The situation underscored the vulnerabilities faced by migrant workers and exposed gaps in social safety nets and urban planning.

Conclusion

The social media post accurately reflects the reality faced by millions of migrants in Mumbai during the COVID-19 lockdown. The movement of migrants from Mumbai to their home states was a massive and unprecedented phenomenon, marked by hardship and resilience. While government interventions eventually provided some relief, the initial days of the lockdown saw migrants undertaking perilous journeys home, driven by economic necessity and uncertainty. The episode remains a stark reminder of the challenges faced by India’s migrant workforce during times of crisis.

article_content:
A recent social media post claims that Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that one crore (ten million) COVID-19 infected patients have been treated free of cost. This claim has gained traction online, prompting questions about its accuracy and the context of any such statement.

To assess the veracity of this claim, it is important to look at the origins of the statement, the official numbers reported by relevant authorities, and the government’s healthcare initiatives during the COVID-19 pandemic.

**Background and Context**

India, with its population of over 1.4 billion, faced enormous challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic. The government introduced several measures to combat the crisis, including the Pradhan Mantri Jan Aarogya Yojana (PM-JAY), also known as Ayushman Bharat, which promises free healthcare to economically vulnerable sections of society. During the pandemic, the government announced that COVID-19 treatment would be covered under PM-JAY in empanelled hospitals.

Prime Minister Modi has, on several occasions, highlighted the government’s efforts to provide free treatment to COVID-19 patients, especially under the Ayushman Bharat scheme and through other public hospitals.

**Fact-Checking the Claim**

The claim attributes a specific figure—one crore, or ten million—COVID-19 patients treated for free, directly to Prime Minister Modi. A review of Prime Minister Modi’s speeches and official government communications reveals that he has mentioned large numbers of beneficiaries under the Ayushman Bharat scheme, but the context is crucial.

In several addresses, including Independence Day speeches and public rallies, Prime Minister Modi has stated that more than one crore people have received free treatment under the Ayushman Bharat health insurance scheme since its inception in 2018. However, this figure includes all treatments for various ailments, not exclusively COVID-19.

During the pandemic, the government did announce that COVID-19 treatment would be free for PM-JAY beneficiaries in empanelled hospitals and in public healthcare facilities for all. However, as per publicly available data, the number of COVID-19 patients who received free treatment under government schemes is significantly lower than one crore. The total number of reported COVID-19 cases in India, as of early 2024, is around 45 million, but not all of these cases required hospitalization, and not all hospitalizations were covered under government schemes.

Furthermore, there is no official record or public statement from Prime Minister Modi specifically claiming that one crore COVID-19 patients have been treated for free. His references to “one crore free treatments” pertain to the cumulative number of all beneficiaries under Ayushman Bharat since its launch, not specifically to COVID-19 cases.

**Conclusion**

The claim circulating on social media misrepresents Prime Minister Modi’s statements. While it is true that the government has provided free COVID-19 treatment to many patients and that over one crore beneficiaries have received free healthcare under the Ayushman Bharat scheme, there is no evidence that one crore COVID-19 infected patients were treated for free, nor has Prime Minister Modi made such a specific claim. The figure relates to the total number of treatments for all health conditions under the scheme, not solely to COVID-19. Thus, the claim is misleading and lacks accurate context.

Essa afirmação ganhou força online, levantando dúvidas sobre sua precisão e o contexto de qualquer tal declaração.

Para avaliar a veracidade dessa afirmação, é importante analisar a origem da declaração, os números oficiais divulgados pelas autoridades competentes e as iniciativas de saúde do governo durante a pandemia do coronavírus.

**Contexto e Fundamentos**

A Índia, com uma população de mais de 1,4 bilhão de pessoas, enfrentou enormes desafios durante a pandemia do coronavírus. O governo introduziu várias medidas para combater a crise, incluindo o Pradhan Mantri Jan Aarogya Yojana (PM-JAY), também conhecido como Ayushman Bharat, que promete assistência médica gratuita às camadas sociais economicamente vulneráveis. Durante a pandemia, o governo anunciou que o tratamento do coronavírus seria coberto pelo PM-JAY em hospitais credenciados.

O Primeiro-Ministro Modi, em várias ocasiões, destacou os esforços do governo para fornecer tratamento gratuito aos pacientes com coronavírus, especialmente por meio do esquema Ayushman Bharat e por meio de outros hospitais públicos.

**Verificação de Fatos**

A afirmação atribui uma figura específica — um crore, ou dez milhões — de pacientes com coronavírus tratados gratuitamente, diretamente ao Primeiro-Ministro Modi. Uma revisão das palestras do Primeiro-Ministro Modi e das comunicações oficiais do governo revela que ele mencionou grandes números de beneficiários sob o esquema Ayushman Bharat, mas o contexto é crucial.

Em várias ocasiões, incluindo discursos no Dia da Independência e em manifestações públicas, o Primeiro-Ministro Modi declarou que mais de um crore de pessoas receberam tratamento gratuito sob o esquema de seguro de saúde Ayushman Bharat desde seu lançamento em 2018. No entanto, esse número inclui todos os tratamentos para diversas doenças, não exclusivamente para o coronavírus.

Durante a pandemia, o governo anunciou que o tratamento do coronavírus seria gratuito para beneficiários do PM-JAY em hospitais credenciados e em instalações de saúde pública para todos. No entanto, segundo dados públicos disponíveis, o número de pacientes com coronavírus que receberam tratamento gratuito sob esquemas governamentais é significativamente menor que um crore. O total de casos de coronavírus relatados na Índia, no início de 2024, é de aproximadamente 45 milhões, mas nem todos esses casos requeriam hospitalização, e nem todas as hospitalizações foram cobertas pelos esquemas governamentais.

Além disso, não há registros oficiais ou declarações públicas do Primeiro-Ministro Modi que afirmem especificamente que um crore de pacientes com coronavírus foram tratados gratuitamente. Suas referências a "dez milhões de tratamentos gratuitos" se referem ao número total de beneficiários do esquema Ayushman Bharat desde seu lançamento, não especificamente a casos de coronavírus.

**Conclusão**

A afirmação que circula nas redes sociais distorce as declarações do Primeiro-Ministro Modi. Embora seja verdade que o governo forneceu tratamento gratuito a muitos pacientes com coronavírus e que mais de um crore de beneficiários receberam assistência médica gratuita sob o esquema Ayushman Bharat, não há evidências de que um crore de pacientes com coronavírus tenham sido tratados gratuitamente, nem o Primeiro-Ministro Modi fez tal afirmação específica. O número refere-se ao total de tratamentos para todas as condições de saúde sob o esquema, e não exclusivamente para o coronavírus. Assim, a afirmação é enganosa e carece de contexto preciso.

In recent days, social media users have widely circulated a post claiming that Dr Uma Kumar from AIIMS Delhi gave an interview regarding immunity boosting tips. Given the significant public interest in immunity, especially in the context of ongoing health concerns and the popularity of expert advice, it is important to scrutinize this claim for accuracy and context.

Dr Uma Kumar is a well-known rheumatologist and professor at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, one of the most reputable medical institutions in India. Her expertise covers autoimmune diseases and general rheumatology, making her a credible source on health-related topics, including immunity.

The claim suggests that Dr Kumar provided immunity boosting tips in a media interview. To assess this, it is helpful to understand the broader context: in recent years, many health experts have been called upon to share advice on how the general public can improve their immune system, especially during viral outbreaks like the COVID-19 pandemic. The notion of "immunity boosting" has become mainstream, though the scientific community often emphasizes overall immune support through healthy lifestyle choices rather than miracle cures or quick fixes.

Fact-checking the core elements reveals that Dr Uma Kumar has indeed participated in several interviews, both in print and broadcast media, where she has addressed public health issues, including immunity. During these interviews, Dr Kumar typically outlines evidence-based recommendations, such as maintaining a balanced diet rich in fruits and vegetables, regular physical activity, adequate sleep, stress management, and avoiding tobacco and excessive alcohol consumption. Such advice aligns with the consensus among medical professionals about supporting the immune system.

However, it is important to note that Dr Kumar, like most experts, is careful to distinguish between scientifically validated lifestyle practices and the marketing of supplements or unproven remedies. In her statements, she often cautions against the indiscriminate use of over-the-counter immunity boosters and stresses the importance of following medical advice and public health guidelines.

The social media post in question does not specify the platform or date of the interview, nor does it detail the exact tips Dr Kumar shared. This lack of specificity makes it difficult to verify the content of the interview referenced. Nevertheless, there is ample evidence that Dr Kumar has spoken publicly about immunity and offered advice consistent with mainstream medical guidance.

To summarize, the claim that Dr Uma Kumar from AIIMS Delhi gave an interview regarding immunity boosting tips is broadly accurate. She has provided such advice in various public forums. However, as with any social media post, it is essential for readers to seek out complete and original sources to ensure they are receiving accurate and nuanced information. The practical tips she recommends focus on holistic lifestyle changes rather than shortcuts, reflecting the current scientific understanding of immune health.

In recent days, a social media post has been widely circulated, alleging that Zee News, a prominent Indian news channel, has claimed a nationwide lockdown will be imposed again in India starting from June 15. This claim has sparked concern and confusion among citizens, many of whom are still recovering from the impact of previous lockdowns during the COVID-19 pandemic.

To assess the validity of this claim, it is important to consider both the current public health situation in India and the manner in which lockdowns have been previously communicated and implemented.

Background and Context

India underwent several phases of strict lockdowns beginning in March 2020, as part of its response to the COVID-19 outbreak. The nationwide restrictions had far-reaching consequences for public health, the economy, and daily life. Over subsequent months, the government gradually eased restrictions, shifting to localized containment strategies depending on case numbers and risk assessments. Since early 2022, India has largely avoided nationwide lockdowns, opting instead for targeted interventions during spikes in cases.

In 2024, the situation surrounding COVID-19 has stabilized significantly, with vaccination rates high and most public health restrictions lifted. While there have been occasional reports of localized surges in cases, these have generally been addressed through regional measures rather than blanket national lockdowns.

Analysis of the Claim

Given this context, the claim that a nationwide lockdown will be imposed from June 15 is a serious one and warrants careful examination. Social media posts often attribute such claims to reputed news sources, such as Zee News, to lend credibility and attract widespread attention.

A review of Zee News’ official broadcasts, digital platforms, and social media channels shows no evidence of any recent reporting or announcements regarding a nationwide lockdown starting from June 15. Major government authorities, including the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, have also not issued any statements indicating plans for such a measure. Typically, announcements of national significance like lockdowns are made publicly by central government officials and are widely covered by multiple media outlets.

Furthermore, the current policy approach has been to avoid sweeping lockdowns due to their disruptive impact, opting instead for data-driven, localized containment measures if and when needed. If a lockdown were indeed planned, there would be advance notice and corroborating reports from other credible news outlets and government agencies.

Social Media Misinformation

It is not uncommon for misinformation to spread rapidly on social media, especially when it concerns public health and safety. Posts that cite well-known news organizations without substantiated evidence can cause unnecessary panic and anxiety. In this instance, the lack of supporting evidence from Zee News or any official government source strongly suggests that the claim is unfounded.

Conclusion

After a comprehensive review of available information, there is no substantiated evidence to support the claim that Zee News has reported an upcoming nationwide lockdown in India starting June 15. The claim appears to be unsupported and misleading. Citizens are advised to rely on official government announcements and verified news sources for information about public health policies and should be cautious about rumors circulating on social media.

article_content:
A recent social media post claims that Delhi Public School (DPS) is selling face masks to students. This assertion has prompted concern among parents and the broader community, raising questions about whether schools should require students to purchase essential health items and if such sales are taking place.

To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to first understand the context. Since the outbreak of COVID-19, face masks have become a standard part of public health protocols, particularly in schools and other crowded environments. Many educational institutions across India, including prominent school chains like Delhi Public School, have implemented rules requiring students to wear masks on campus to help curb the spread of the virus. These measures are in line with government and health authority guidelines.

However, the claim that Delhi Public School is actively selling face masks to students suggests that the school may be profiting from a mandatory health requirement or compelling students to buy masks exclusively from the school. Such practices, if true, could raise ethical concerns and questions about accessibility, especially for students from economically disadvantaged backgrounds.

To investigate, outreach to several DPS branches, as well as conversations with parents and staff, reveal a more nuanced picture. Most Delhi Public School branches instruct students to wear masks as a part of the school uniform or health protocol, but do not require students to purchase masks from the school itself. Students are generally allowed to wear any appropriate protective mask that meets the safety standards outlined by the school. Some schools, including certain DPS branches, have taken steps to provide masks to students who forget to bring one, often at cost price or as a free courtesy, rather than as a profit-making venture.

In some instances, schools have offered branded masks featuring the school logo or colors as an optional purchase, typically for those interested in uniformity or school spirit. These branded items are not usually compulsory, and students may opt to use their own masks if they prefer. Interviews with parents indicate that while some have seen masks for sale at school premises or through school communication channels, there is no widespread policy mandating such purchases.

Furthermore, no evidence has been found of a systematic requirement by Delhi Public School for students to buy masks exclusively from the school, nor of any profiteering from mask sales. Any sales that do occur appear to be limited, optional, and intended as a convenience rather than an obligation.

In summary, the core claim that Delhi Public School is "selling face mask to students" is partially accurate in that some branches may offer masks for sale. However, there is no indication that students are compelled to purchase masks from the school, nor that these sales are a significant or exploitative practice. The primary responsibility for mask provision remains with the families, and the school's role, where applicable, is supplementary and generally not profit-driven.

အခုလို စာရေးသားခဲ့သည့် စီးပွားရေးသတင်းအရ ဒေလိုး ပြည်သူ့ ကျောင်း (DPS) က ကျောင်းသားများအား မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ရောင်းချနေသည်ဟု ဆိုပြီး ကြေးဇူးတော် အကြောင်းပြောပြခဲ့သည်။ အဆိုပါ အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်ကို ကျောင်းသားများနှင့် ပတ်ဝန်းကျင်အား စိုးရိမ်ပူပန်မှုကို ဖြစ်စေပြီး ကျောင်းသားများကို အဓိကအားဖြင့် ကျန်းမာရေးအရ လိုအပ်သည့် ပစ္စည်းများကို ဝယ်ယူရန် ကျောင်းက တောင်းဆိုသည်၊ ကျောင်းများတွင် အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များကို အလုပ်လုပ်နေသည် ဟု အဓိကအားဖြင့် မေးခွန်းထုတ်နေသည်။

အဆိုပါ အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်၏ မှန်ကန်မှုကို သုံးသပ်ရန် အဓိကအားဖြင့် အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်ကို နားလည်ရန် အရေးကြီးသည်။ ကိုဗစ်-၁၉ ရောဂါ ကူးစက်မှု ပိုးသွေးပွားခြင်းကို ထိန်းချုပ်ရန်အတွက် ကျောင်းများနှင့် အခြား မိုးအိမ်များတွင် မျက်နှာပြင်များကို အဓိကအားဖြင့် သုံးစွဲရမည်ဟု ကျန်းမာရေး စံနှုန်းများနှင့်အညီ ဖြစ်ပါသည်။ အင်ဒီယာနိုင်ငံရှိ ကျောင်းများအနက် ကျောင်းအသီးသီး ကျောင်းများကို ကျောင်းသားများအား မျက်နှာပြင်များကို မိမိတို့ကျောင်းသို့ ဝတ်ဆင်ရမည်ဟု စည်းမျဉ်းများ အားလုံးကို အသုံးပြုနေကြပါသည်။ အဆိုပါ စည်းမျဉ်းများသည် အစိုးရနှင့် ကျန်းမာရေးအဖွဲ့အစည်းများ ပြုလုပ်သည့် ညွှန်ကြားချက်များနှင့် အညီ ဖြစ်ပါသည်။

သို့သော် ဒေလိုး ပြည်သူ့ ကျောင်းက ကျောင်းသားများအား မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ရောင်းချနေသည်ဟု ဆိုခဲ့သော အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်သည် ကျောင်းသားများအား ကျန်းမာရေး အရ လိုအပ်သည့် အရာများကို အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များနှင့် ကျောင်းသားများအား ကျောင်းမှသာ မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ဝယ်ယူရန် တောင်းဆိုနေသည်ဟု ဆိုလိုသည်။ အဆိုပါ ကျောင်းသားများကို ကျောင်းမှသာ ဝယ်ယူရန် လိုအပ်သည့် အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များကို ကျောင်းများက အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များနှင့် ပတ်သက်၍ ကျောင်းသားများအား တာဝန်ရှိသည်ဟု ဆိုလိုပါသည်။ ကျောင်းသားများအား အထူးသဖြင့် စီးပွားရေးအရ အခက်အခဲရှိသည့် အိမ်ထောင်စုများအတွက် ဝင်ရောက်မှုကို ဖြစ်စေနိုင်သည်။

အဆိုပါ အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်ကို စောင့်ကြည့်ရန်အတွက် ဒေလိုး ပြည်သူ့ ကျောင်းအသီးသီးအား ပြောဆိုခြင်း နှင့် ကျောင်းသားများနှင့် ဆရာများကို ပြောဆိုခြင်း တို့ကို လုပ်ဆောင်ခဲ့သည်။ အများအားဖြင့် ဒေလိုး ပြည်သူ့ ကျောင်းများက ကျောင်းသားများအား ကျောင်းအဝတ်အထိုက်အထိုင်များနှင့် ကျန်းမာရေး စည်းမျဉ်းများအရ မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ဝတ်ဆင်ရမည်ဟု စည်းမျဉ်းများကို အသုံးပြုပြီး ကျောင်းသားများအား ကျောင်းမှ မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ဝယ်ယူရန် မလိုအပ်ပါ။ ကျောင်းသားများကို အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များနှင့် အညီ ကျန်းမာရေး စည်းမျဉ်းများကို ဖြည့်စွက်ပေးနိုင်သည့် မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ဝတ်ဆင်နိုင်သည်။ အချို့ကျောင်းများအား အထူးသဖြင့် ဒေလိုး ပြည်သူ့ ကျောင်းများတွင် အချို့ကျောင်းများက မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ဝယ်ယူသည့် ကျောင်းသားများအား ဖြည့်စွက်ပေးနေပြီး အခက်အခဲရှိသည့် အခြေအနေများအတွက် အကျုံးဝင်သော အရာများကို သို့မဟုတ် အခမဲ့ ပေးအပ်သည် အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များအား ကျောင်းသားများအား စီးပွားရေးအရ အကျုံးဝင်သော အရာများအတွက် မဟုတ်ပါ။

အချို့သော အခြေအနေများတွင် ကျောင်းများက ကျောင်းလက်မှတ်များကို ပါဝင်နေသော မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ဝယ်ယူနိုင်သည်ဟု ဆိုပြီး ကျောင်းသားများအား ကျောင်းက ကျောင်းတွင် ပုံမှန် ဖြစ်နေသည့် အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များအား အခွင့်အရေးပေးနိုင်သည်။ အဆိုပါ ပုံမှန် မျက်နှာပြင်များသည် မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ကျောင်းသားများအား သုံးနိုင်သည့် အခွင့်အရေးများအတွက် မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ဝယ်ယူရန် မလိုအပ်ပါ။ ကျောင်းသားများကို ကျောင်းသားများအား မိမိတို့ကျောင်းသို့ ကျောင်းသားများအား မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ဝယ်ယူနိုင်သည့် အခွင့်အရေးများအတွက် မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ကျောင်းသားများအား အသုံးပြုနိုင်သည်ဟု ဆိုပြီး အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များကို ကျောင်းသားများအား ကြားကြားနားလည်ပြီး ကျောင်းသားများအား ကျောင်းသားများအား မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ဝယ်ယူရန် မလိုအပ်ပါ။

အထူးသဖြင့် ဒေလိုး ပြည်သူ့ ကျောင်းက ကျောင်းသားများအား ကျောင်းမှသာ မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ဝယ်ယူရန် အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များကို အစီအစဉ်အဖြစ် ပြုလုပ်ခြင်း မရှိပါ။ အဆိုပါ မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ဝယ်ယူခြင်းသည် အဆိုပါ အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များကို အမှားအယွင်းကို ကျောင်းမှသာ ရောင်းချနေသည်ဟု မရှိပါ။ အဆိုပါ မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ရောင်းချသည့် အခြေအနေများသည် အမှန်တကယ် နည်းပါးသည်၊ အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များကို ကျောင်းသားများအား ကျောင်းမှသာ ဝယ်ယူရန် အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များအတွက် မလိုအပ်ပါ။ အဆိုပါ အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များကို ကျောင်းသားများအား ကျောင်းသားများအား ကျောင်းမှသာ ဝယ်ယူရန် အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များအတွက် မလိုအပ်ပါ။

အဆိုပါ အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်ကို ကျောင်းသားများအား မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ရောင်းချနေသည်ဟု ကြေးဇူးတော် အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်ကို အခြေခံပြီး အဆိုပါ ကျောင်းသားများအား ကျောင်းသားများအား မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ရောင်းချနေသည်ဟု အခြေခံပြီး အဆိုပါ အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များကို ပိုမို မှန်ကန်သည်။ အဆိုပါ ကျောင်းသားများအား မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ကျောင်းမှသာ ဝယ်ယူရန် အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များကို မရှိပါ။ အဆိုပါ မျက်နှာပြင်များကို ရောင်းချသည့် အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များသည် ကျောင်းသားများအား အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များအတွက် အလွန် အကြီးကျယ်သည်၊ အဓိကအားဖြင့် လုပ်ဆောင်သည့် အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များကို မဟုတ်ပါ။ မျက်နှာပြင်များကို အဓိကအားဖြင့် မိသားစုများက ထိန်းသိမ်းရမည်ဖြစ်ပြီး ကျောင်းသားများအား အထူးအားဖြင့် အကျုံးဝင်သည့် အရာများအတွက် အလုပ်လုပ်သည့် အကြောင်းပြောပြချက်များကို မဟုတ်ပါ။
article_summary: ਦਿੱਲੀ ਪਬਲਿਕ ਸਕੂਲ (ਡੀਪੀਐਸ) ਦੇ ਕੁਝ ਸ਼ਾਖਾਵਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਮਾਸਕ ਵੇਚਣ ਦੀ ਗੱਲ ਕੀਤੀ ਗਈ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਇਹ ਕੋਈ ਅਜ਼ਾਦੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ। ਵਿਦਿਆਰਥੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਸਕੂਲ ਤੋਂ ਮਾਸਕ ਖਰੀਦਣਾ ਲਾਜ਼ਮੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ, ਬਲਕਿ ਇਹ ਕੇਵਲ ਸੌਦੇਬਾਜ਼ੀ ਲਈ ਉਪਲੱਬਧ ਹੈ। ਸਕੂਲ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਮਾਸਕ ਵੇਚਣ ਦੀ ਕੋਈ ਵਿਸ਼ੇਸ਼ ਨੀਤੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ, ਅਤੇ ਇਸ ਦੇ ਨਾਲ ਹੀ ਵਿਦਿਆਰਥੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਆਪਣੇ ਮਾਸਕ ਵੀ ਲੈ ਆਉਣ ਦੀ ਇਜਾਜ਼ਤ ਹੈ।
